clue.text: Birdie, you fly alarmingly close to a road

parts.note: to buzz an aircraft or person is to fly dangerously near them

explanation.surface: A bird is warned off swooping too near a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzard is a large hawk, so it is a 'birdie' in the clue's playful diminutive.

clue.text: Adulterous spa lady of degree

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the biblical woman known for her adultery

parts.note: Bath is the English spa city
she is the pronoun for a woman
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A woman of rank at a spa town commits adultery.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a Somerset city famous for its Roman spa.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible David's affair with Uriah's wife makes her the archetypal adulteress.

clue.text: Regent's Park porcelain going up fast

parts.note: London Zoo stands in Regent's Park
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: China in a London park rockets in value.
explanation.walkthrough: Regent's Park is a royal park in north London, home of London Zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices or aircraft that soar rapidly are said to climb steeply.

clue.text: Tutti

parts.note: an Italian musical direction for every performer to play together

explanation.definitionFit: The musical term tells the whole ensemble to sound simultaneously.

clue.text: Cromwellian tumbler

parts.note: a tumbler sounds like an acrobat or glass, but it is Oliver's son Richard, who soon fell from power

explanation.surface: An acrobat or drinking glass from Cromwell's time.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Cromwell, Lord Protector after his father, was mocked as 'Tumbledown Dick' when he quickly fell.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form of Richard was the mocking name for Oliver's son who tumbled from office.

clue.text: Doubtful of the lass, beamish boy as you return?

parts.note: a gal is an informal word for a girl or lass
umph, like humph, is the grunt of someone doubtful or unconvinced

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical of a girl asks a cheerful lad how he'll come back.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky the 'beamish boy' slays the beast and 'went galumphing back', so the definition describes how he returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll coined the verb for the triumphant, clumsy bounding home of the hero of his nonsense poem.

clue.text: A prominent feature is applied to this by industry

definitions.text: A prominent feature is applied to this by industry

parts.words: A prominent feature is applied to this by industry
parts.note: the prominent feature is the nose, kept to a stone for sharpening when one works hard

explanation.surface: Manufacturers fit a striking component to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'nose to the grindstone' means working diligently; industry here is hard work, not manufacturing.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving stone wheel sharpens tools, and diligence is pictured as keeping the nose against it.

clue.text: Catch one of Burns's rash " girls

definitions.meaning: to snare with a noosed rope
Burns's song Green Grow the Rashes, O ends lines with 'lasses, O', so one is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A noosed rope catches cattle, and Burns's refrain 'the lasses, O' supplies a single girl with her O.

clue.text: She accused her fiance of cheating at chess

definitions.text: She accused her fiance of cheating at chess

parts.words: She accused her fiance of cheating at chess
parts.note: in Shakespeare's The Tempest, Prospero's daughter tells Ferdinand over the chessboard that he plays her false

explanation.surface: A woman alleges her intended cheated during a chess game.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero's daughter in The Tempest is discovered playing chess with Ferdinand.

clue.text: Had incomplete shop edition of Great Expectations ?

definitions.note: a noun phrase, with the clue's 'Had' turning it into the past-tense verb sense

indicators.note: neither the word shop nor edition is used whole: the answer is the run straddling them

explanation.surface: Someone owned a defective bookshop copy of the Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: To have had great expectations is to have wished for something; 'Had' joins the novel's title to give that verb sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking forward with confident desire is what having big expectations amounts to.

clue.text: Sing a catch or spin for one

definitions.meaning: to sing a round or catch in turn, an old sense of the verb
fishing by trailing a spinning bait behind a boat is one kind of this angling method

explanation.definitionFit: The verb once meant singing a part-song in succession, and in angling it means drawing a baited line through water.

clue.text: Tommy's Colonel might indeed have felt a tightness about the head

definitions.text: Tommy's Colonel might indeed have felt a tightness about the head

parts.words: Tommy's Colonel might indeed have felt a tightness about the head
parts.note: a soldier's officer feeling something tight round his head sounds like a headache, but it is the strap of his helmet under the jaw

explanation.surface: A British soldier's commanding officer suffers a tension headache.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap fastened beneath the jaw holds a helmet or cap tight to the head.

clue.text: Restricts daily tasks

definitions.meaning: to limit or skimp on supply, as in rationing
allotted periods or shares of work

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for limiting supply and a noun for an allotted spell of work.

clue.text: Despite Anno Domini enlisted, being neighbourly

definitions.note: describes a state, matching an adjectival past participle

parts.note: AD is the abbreviation for Anno Domini, in the year of our Lord
someone who enlisted joined up with the forces

explanation.surface: Though old, a man signs up for the army and is friendly to those nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despite' is a link word playing on 'Anno Domini' as old age: joining up in spite of advancing years.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that lie next to each other share a border, as neighbours do.

clue.text: Something fishy in the harvest. Flora

parts.note: corn is the grain crop gathered at harvest
a cockle is an edible shellfish, loosely something fishy

explanation.surface: Something suspicious turns up among the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a purple-flowered weed of cornfields, a plant and so part of the flora.

clue.text: As the Spanish request Dutch spirit that's Scotch ?

definitions.note: the question mark marks a place name standing in for the adjective Scottish

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article, 'the'
gin descends from Dutch genever, a juniper spirit

explanation.surface: Like Spaniards, someone orders Dutch liquor and calls it whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: ELGIN is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland, hence Scotch; the surface wants whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral town lies in Moray in the Scottish north-east.

clue.text: The only man able to jolt Boney?

definitions.text: The only man able to jolt Boney?

parts.words: The only man able to jolt Boney?
parts.note: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon, but here it means a bony patient whose skeleton a manipulating practitioner adjusts

explanation.surface: Who alone could shake up Napoleon?
explanation.walkthrough: Boney was the British nickname for Napoleon Bonaparte, so the clue reads as military history.
explanation.definitionFit: This practitioner treats ailments by manipulating the bones and joints of the body.

clue.text: Right mistress, sound doctrine

parts.note: ortho- is a prefix meaning right or correct
a doxy is an archaic word for a mistress

explanation.surface: Correct moral teaching about keeping a mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepted, correct belief is what established teaching is held to be.

clue.text: Flower of Christmassy wine?

parts.note: holly is the evergreen of Christmas decorations
hock is German white wine

explanation.surface: A festive bloom made from seasonal wine.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK is the British name for German Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tall garden plant bearing large showy blooms on spikes.

clue.text: General using wheeled "cavalry" for victory?

parts.note: the quoted cavalry is the wooden horse, rolled into Troy, that won the war for the commander of the Greeks

explanation.surface: A commander wins a battle with mounted troops on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Greek host at Troy, which fell through the ruse of the wooden horse.

clue.text: Tenderly, little Rosalind, in a low voice

indicators.note: the shortened name is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: a moo is the lowing of a cow, a low voice in pun
Ros is a short form of the name Rosalind

explanation.surface: A girl speaks softly and affectionately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is a cow's call, not quiet: the wordplay is A MOO with ROS put in.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian musical direction to play lovingly and with tenderness.

clue.text: Whole lot of adders

definitions.meaning: the sum that people adding up figures arrive at

explanation.definitionFit: The word means complete as an adjective and a sum reached by addition as a noun.

clue.text: Old Master could draw game

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A great painter was capable of drawing a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century Venetian painter ranks among the great European artists.

clue.text: Hyde Park oratory? No, but not far off

definitions.text: Hyde Park oratory? No, but not far off

parts.words: Hyde Park oratory? No, but not far off
parts.note: the oratory suggests soapbox speeches at Speakers' Corner, but the church meant stands a short way from the park in Knightsbridge

explanation.surface: Is this the speechmaking in Hyde Park? Not quite, but close.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner in Hyde Park is London's spot for public oratory; the Brompton Oratory is a Catholic church nearby in South Kensington.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district gives its name to the famous Catholic church, the Oratory, near Hyde Park.

clue.text: Handsome and approachable?

definitions.meaning: playfully read as '...', able to come near

explanation.definitionFit: The word means attractive in looks, and split jokily it suggests a person one can come towards.

clue.text: Foundations of many a character

parts.note: character suggests personality, but the characters are printed letters, formed from writing fluids

explanation.surface: What builds the basis of a person's nature.

clue.text: Ticket to Reading

explanation.surface: A rail fare to the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town west of London on the main railway line, so the capital letter suggests a train journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift voucher redeemable at a bookshop pays for reading material.

clue.text: Zero volume, zero decoration

parts.note: the figure nought looks like the letter O
nought again gives a second O

explanation.surface: Silence and nothing to adorn the place: a bare, empty room.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a convex rounded moulding used as ornament in classical architecture.

clue.text: Function of cupboard at home or in the theatre

indicators.note: the word or is placed within the word for the theatre

parts.note: the stage is the theatrical profession

explanation.surface: A cupboard serves a purpose at home or as a prop on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping things put away is what a cupboard is for in a household.

clue.text: He sought fleshly satisfaction

parts.note: fleshly hints at lust, but the man meant demanded a literal pound of flesh as settlement of a debt

explanation.surface: A man pursued carnal pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice the moneylender claims a pound of Antonio's flesh as his bond.
